name: Watermelon Fusarium Wilt
description: A soil-borne fungal disease that causes wilting and death of watermelon plants. The pathogen is specific to watermelon and persists in soil for many years, making it difficult to manage.
symptoms: Yellowing of lower leaves progressing upward
Wilting of leaves and vines during hot part of day
Progressive decline leading to plant death
Brown to black discoloration of roots and crown
causes: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. niveum fungus
Soil-borne pathogen entering through root tips
High soil temperatures favoring disease development
treatments: No effective cure once plant is infected
Adjust soil pH to 6.5-7.0 with lime
prevention: Practice long crop rotation (5+ years) with non-cucurbits
Use raised beds to improve drainage
